newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise but trade seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise but trade seen limited.

text.p: Danish bond prices edged up slightly on Wednesday, but dealers expected trade to be limited by a lack of key data and continuing worries about EMU.
"There are no new indicators on the way from the United States or Germany. On Wednesday we shall again be keeping an eye out for new statements on Emu," a dealer said.

At 0800 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 stood at 111.50, yielding 6.24 percent, up from Tuesday's 111.24.The seven percent 2007 bond, which becomes the benchmark on September 1, was up 0.17 point, at 104.19, yielding 6.44 percent.
The 2006 benchmark's 10-year yield gap with Germany shrunk to 47 basis points from Tuesday's 50 bp. The seven percent 2007-bund differential was one bp narrower, at 67.
The 2006 bond's June future rose 0.28 point to 111.50 and the six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.15 point to 89.55.
The crown was unchanged at 3.8075 per mark. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33-969650
